explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses the hardness–strength–plasticity tradeoff and proposes a controlled, falsifiable SRO-based mechanism. E2 and E3 support the general premise that chemical ordering can raise barriers to dislocation motion, but neither establishes that equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is initially random with minimal SRO or that annealing at 700–800 °C can vary SRO while retaining an otherwise unchanged single-phase microstructure. E1 mainly concerns partial-dislocation, planar-slip, and twinning mechanisms and provides little direct support for the proposed premise. Annealing could also change grain size, residual stress, segregation, or precipitate secondary phases, so stronger controls are needed to isolate SRO. Relative to the hidden target, the proposal does not reconstruct high-energy ball milling, SPS, nanocrystalline grain refinement, densification, or the 83% FCC/17% BCC structure. It also omits the target processing window and quantitative outcomes of approximately 675 Hv, 1894 MPa compressive strength, and 1238 MPa yield stress. Thus it is scientifically plausible as an alternative explanation, but it has little agreement with the target intervention, conditions, structural mediator, and measured result.
